foundation.q: Write every factor of 24 (every whole number that divides 24 exactly).
foundation.work: All eight needed for the mark. Common error: missing 8 or 12, or stopping at 6. Skill used in Lessons 2 and 8.
Divide top and bottom by 6. Common error: 3/18 or 2/12 (not fully simplified). Skill used in Lessons 6 and 9.

foundation.q: Two angles of a triangle are 52 and 63 degrees. What is the third angle, in degrees?
foundation.work: Angle sum is 180. Common error: using 360 or an arithmetic slip. Skill used in Lesson 7.

foundation.q: Read this little program. Start with n = 5. Then repeat 4 times: change n by 3 (add 3 to n). At the end, say n. What does it say?
foundation.work: 5, 8, 11, 14, 17. Common error: 20 (adding 3 five times) or 12 (adding 3 only once). Not a mark against the child: this also shows how ready they are for the coding side, so the tutor can plan support.

core.q: A number machine doubles the input and then adds 5. The output is 31. What was the input?
core.work: Look for working backwards (31 - 5, then halve). Common error: halving first or giving 26.

core.q: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. For example, 7 is prime, but 9 is not (its factors are 1, 3 and 9). How many prime numbers are there between 30 and 50?
core.work: Primes are 31, 37, 41, 43, 47. Common errors: including 39 or 49, or counting 1.

core.q: The temperature is -4 degrees C at night. It rises by 9 degrees by noon, then falls by 12 degrees by evening. What is the evening temperature in degrees C?
core.work: Check number line use: -4 + 9 = 5, 5 - 12 = -7. Common error: answering 7.

core.q: A bag has 4 red, 3 blue and 5 green marbles. One marble is picked without looking. The chance (probability) of picking blue is 3 out of 12, written 3/12. What is the probability that it is NOT green? Give a fraction in simplest form.
core.work: Total is 12, not green is 7. Common error: 5/12, or 7/5 (comparing to green).

core.q: The average of 5 numbers is 12. Four of the numbers are 8, 10, 15 and 11. What is the fifth number?
core.work: Total must be 60 (5 x 12); the four add to 44. Common error: finding the average of the four numbers. Some children say 'mean' for average; both are fine.

core.q: It is 10 o'clock now on a 12-hour clock. What time will it be 17 hours later? Give the hour only.
core.work: 10 + 17 = 27, 27 - 24 = 3 (or 17 mod 12 = 5, then 10 + 5 = 15 -> 3). Common error: answering 27 or 5.

stretch.q: The pattern 4, 7, 10, 13, ... carries on in the same way. What is the 50th number? Explain how you worked it out.
stretch.work: Rule: 4 + 3 x 49 = 151 (the 50th number has 49 jumps of 3). Accept any clear method. Common error: 150 (3 x 50) or 154 (4 + 3 x 50). A flag for the Think harder pages, not a mark against the child.

stretch.q: Using the digits 1, 2, 3 and 4, with no digit used more than once, how many different 3-digit even numbers can be made?
stretch.work: Last digit 2 or 4 (2 ways), then 3 x 2 for the others. Common error: 24 (ignoring evenness) or listing incompletely. A flag for the Think harder pages, not a mark against the child.

tutorKey: Finished very fast? Ask the child to explain one answer aloud before you mark: a fast wrong answer is often a skipped step, not a missing topic. The parent makes the final choice.
